title: RevokeUserSessions
description: The body of an administrative bulk session revocation, derived from identity_application::administration::RevokeUserSessions. This is the ADMINISTRATOR's version of signing someone out everywhere, and it is a SEPARATE TYPE from the self-service RevokeAllSessions on purpose: a confused deputy that let a user pass a user_id to the self-service command would be an account-takeover primitive, so the two are different types with different fields.
x-serde-status: the type is IMPLEMENTED as a shape; RevokeUserSessionsCommand has no body and no route serves it

context.description: Who is asking, and under which session. Required at AAL2.

user_id.description: The user whose sessions are revoked. The whole reason this is a different type from the self-service command.

reason.description: Why, recorded in the audit trail. Mandatory and non-empty.

x-distinct-from-suspension: Revoking sessions ends the user's current access WITHOUT changing their account status; suspending changes their status and revokes sessions as a consequence. Collapsing them into one 'disable the user' button would be imprecise about which thing an operator did, and both are written to the audit trail.
x-the-o1-alternative: This command walks sessions; bumping the user's security_version achieves the same result in O(1) without enumerating them, which is the mechanism Phase 1 is built around. Both write the all_sessions_revoked audit event. Which one this route uses is a Phase 6 decision, and this contract does not claim it is settled.
x-phase: Phase 1 — Sessions and the request context for the mechanism, Phase 6 — Administration for the administrative surface
